Clients expect direct contact details, prompt responses, regular updates and convenient access to information as a normal part of working with a law firm. ## First impressions still matter, but consistency matters more

Initial contact with law firms remains dominated by phone calls, which are still the most common first point of contact overall at 43%. This is followed by email at 22%, meeting in person at 14% and walking into the office at 11%. [...] Younger clients continue to raise the bar on digital access. Among those aged 18 to 29, 67% said online chat was important and 75% said 24/7 access was important. Older clients are less focused on always-on access, but still place strong value on reliability, clarity and human reassurance.

hits.title: Client Communication for Law Firms | The Access Group
hits.snippet:
Clients have different preferences for communication style or frequency. Some expect instant app updates, while others favour phone calls or scheduled emails. Ignoring these preferences can frustrate clients, generate repeated queries about what’s happening, and strain relationships. [...] Many law firms struggle with inconsistent follow-ups, email overload, fragmented contacts, remote collaboration challenges, and security concerns. Silence often leads to anxiety, which quickly escalates to complaints and negative reviews. Proactive, predictable updates can dramatically reduce calls asking for case updates, keeping clients informed and confident throughout their legal journey. This approach also frees up fee-earners to focus on delivering legal advice and progressing cases [...] ### How often should a law firm update clients on their matter?

Requirements and preferences for communication vary by client and by case. However, law firms should aim to set a predictable schedule for client updates that fee earners can realistically follow. Regular updates reduce anxiety and complaints, and automated client follow-ups can help to ensure consistency without adding to staff workload.

hits.title: Legal client portal software: 4 reasons it's a go-to solution | Legal Solutions UK | Thomson Reuters
hits.snippet:
When a client needs to get ahold of their lawyer, what do they do? Send an email? Call the firm’s front desk? What about the lawyer’s direct line or cell phone? In some cases, a client will try any and maybe all of these options — and the lawyer is left having to respond to every single one, wasting valuable time.

Law firm client portal software can fix this problem by creating one private location for clients and lawyers to communicate. There are many advantages to this: [...] Faster and easier communication:With a centralised location, client portals simplify things since lawyers no longer have to monitor multiple methods of communication (i.e. email, cell phone, direct line, voicemail) - and keeping everything in one spot means improved responsiveness. [...] No longer must you schedule client appointments and phone calls to discuss each and every detail of the case. You can do it all in the client portal. It simplifies and streamlines the collaboration process, plain and simple.

And speaking of collaboration, your client can do it on their schedule, 24 hours a day. Whether it’s 2 am, 2 pm, or any time in between, clients can access, review, and provide feedback on any of the documents related to their case – from any device.
